synthesis.explanation:
Short answer: the bot doesn't see the -50 from either card. It plays Metal Core Barrier for an unrelated reason, and Jasmine gets nothing from that reason.

1. The search never plays out the opponent's turn. kp3 looks 3 moves ahead on its own turn only (opponent_ply 0). It scores the position the moment its turn ends (expectiminimax_player.rs:914-918). Both -50s only matter when the opponent attacks, and that attack is never simulated. The scoring's threat clock divides raw HP by the attacker's damage (value_functions.rs:905, 941), so it ignores reductions. Even the kd pilot's defender pricing leaves out Metal Core Barrier and turn effects on purpose (hooks/core.rs:1577-1580).

2. Why the Tool gets played anyway: the score adds a flat +10 whenever your Active holds any Tool (value_functions.rs:50, 516, 667-672). It doesn't check which Tool it is or whether the holder is Metal. Each card that leaves your hand costs 1 point (lines 45, 510). So Metal Core Barrier on the Active nets +9, while Jasmine nets -1, the same as a Tool on the Bench.
- **The Indeedee ex evidence:** the bot put Metal Core Barrier on a Psychic Indeedee ex Active 57 to 63 times per 240 games. The Barrier does nothing there, and that attach still scored exactly +10 over the Bench at 25 of 25 decisions.
- **The causal test (same 240 seeds):** with the +10 set to 0, Metal Core Barrier dropped from 74.6% of its turns to 1.5%, and Steel Apron from 70.5% to 2.7%. Giving Jasmine's stored effect the same +10 raised Jasmine from 1.8% to 82.4%.

3. Jasmine is held because it scores 1 lower, not because the bot judged it and turned it down. At all 191 decisions where the bot ended its turn with Jasmine playable, Jasmine scored exactly 1.0 lower (the card-in-hand point). On 439 to 535 turns per 240 games, it played no Supporter at all.

4. The rare real Jasmine plays are an accident. The opponent's Hiking Trail refills your hand to 3 at the end of your turn, so playing any card draws one, and the smaller deck scores +1 (value_functions.rs:511). Of the 10 real plays examined, 9 were against Blaziken, the only list with Hiking Trail. One play against Altaria is unexplained.

5. The engine is correct. Both cards cut a 150 hit on Skarmory ex to 100, at the same step after Weakness and for the same turn. Jasmine actually covers more: it also protects a benched or switched-in Skarmory ex, and it stacks with Steel Apron. The Tool costs no Supporter slot.

6. The Tools still help, even though the bot plays them for the wrong reason. Removing the +10 cut deck 07's wins from 132 to 97 of 240, and every matchup went down. Pricing Jasmine gave 146 of 240 (+5.8 points), which is within noise at 240 games.

synthesis.implications:
For deck 07:
- The simulator's Jasmine numbers say nothing about how good Jasmine is. The bot never scores the -50, so Jasmine's 1.3% floor play rate and the deck's 47.3% floor both come from a pilot that treats Jasmine as a dead card.
- The Metal Core Barrier numbers aren't evidence either. About 1 in 5 Barriers go onto Indeedee ex for nothing, and when both Tools fit, the Barrier beats Steel Apron only on move order.
- When Dustin plays the ladder by hand, the reasonable reading (an inference, not measured) is: Jasmine is worth playing on a turn with no better Supporter, when Skarmory ex is Active and facing a hit of 50 or more. Metal Core Barrier should go only on a [M] Pokemon.
- Whether putting Jasmine in the bot's scoring actually raises the win rate is unproven. The +5.8 points in variant B is within noise at 240 games.

For other decks:
- The +10 is blind to what the Tool does, so any deck with Tools will see the bot put any Tool on its Active, even where the Tool does nothing for that Pokemon. Win rates for Tool-heavy decks are partly driven by this term.
- Any Supporter whose only payoff is a stored effect during the opponent's turn gets nothing but the -1 hand cost. The bot will hold it unless the opponent's Hiking Trail (or a similar refill) accidentally makes dumping a card worth +1. floor.py already flags this category; the flag is correct.

Possible fixes (none built into the official pilot; each would be a new pilot and needs its own A/B at 1,920 games, Dustin's call):
1. Price the real reductions. Extend kd's persistent_defender_damage, or the threat clock, to count Metal Core Barrier and ReducedDamageForTarget turn effects that cover the defender during the opponent's next turn. This is the principled fix, and it would also retire the card-blind bonus.
2. Make active_has_tool card-aware: count a Tool only if its effect applies to its holder. That would stop the Indeedee ex attaches.
3. Variant B, the blunt version already tested: +10 for Jasmine's effect while it covers the Active. Jasmine went to 82.4% and wins to 146/240, which is noise-level.
4. Do not simply zero the +10: that cost about 15 points of win rate (132 -> 97 of 240), because the Tools do help once played.

Separately, and not affecting 07: the engine's Metal Core Barrier is missing the attacker-is-opponent gate that rules/09 H2 calls for.

result.summary:
Short answer: the bot doesn't understand the -50 from either card. It plays Metal Core Barrier because its scoring gives a flat +10 whenever its Active Pokemon is holding any Tool. That bonus ignores what the Tool does. Nothing in its scoring reads Jasmine's effect, so Jasmine only ever shows up as one fewer card in hand, which scores -1.

How kp3 scores these plays (value_functions.rs):
- Card in hand: +1 per card (weight at line 45, used at line 510).
- Tool on the Active: +10 (weight at line 50, used at line 516). `get_active_has_tool` (667-672) returns 1 if the Active has anything attached (played_card.rs:336-338). It does not look at the Tool's name or effect, or whether the Pokemon is Metal.
- Net result: any Tool onto the Active is +9. A Tool onto a Benched Pokemon is -1. Jasmine is -1.

What never reads either card:
- The threat clock divides raw HP by the attacker's damage (lines 905 and 941) and ignores reductions. kp3 runs with the kd feature off (421-431, 248-252).
- Even kd's defender pricing leaves out Metal Core Barrier and turn effects on purpose (hooks/core.rs:1577-1580). It does read Steel Apron (1615).
- Public pricing changes nothing for either card. Neither text mentions the opponent's hand or deck (observation.rs:478-490), and neither is in AUDITED_TEXTS. For these two cards, kp3 plays exactly like k3.

The search: it looks 3 actions ahead on its own turn only. A Tool costs 2 of those 3 actions (play the card, then choose where to attach it), which leaves exactly one for the attack. Jasmine costs 1. An attack ends the turn without using up an action (expectiminimax_player.rs:633-657). The position is then scored at the start of the opponent's turn, with no opponent move played out (773-798). Both effects are still live in the game state at that point; the scoring just doesn't read them.

A scratch test (seed 21,102,000,001) matched all of this exactly. The engine itself applies both cards correctly: against a 150-damage attack, Jasmine and Metal Core Barrier each leave Skarmory ex at 40 HP, while no card or Steel Apron gets it knocked out. So the rules are right and the bot's scoring is what's wrong.

Why Jasmine still got played 50 times (inference, not measured): I found one way it can win. If the bot can prove the opponent wins outright when the turn simply ends, that line scores -100,000. Playing any Trainer other than X Speed voids that proof, so Jasmine escapes the penalty when it's the only such play available. That was confirmed in a built position, but it is probably rare in this deck: the proof refuses boards with Indeedee ex in play, any Tool other than Giant Cape, Starting Plains, or Steel Wing's effect.

result.summary:
The +10 is the cause. kp3's evaluator gives +10 whenever the Active Pokemon has any Tool attached. It never looks at the -50 from either card. I removed that +10 in a scratch build, and Metal Core Barrier went from 74.6% of its turns to 1.5%. Steel Apron fell from 70.5% to 2.7%. When I instead gave Jasmine's stored effect the same +10 (only while it protects the Active), Jasmine rose from 1.8% to 82.4%.

How it works: kp3 uses public_clock_effect_value_function with the baseline() parameter set (mod.rs:502-511, value_functions.rs:176-187). The only weight that matters is line 50. Line 82 belongs to variant(), which kp3 never uses. The score line (value_functions.rs:516) adds (my.active_has_tool - opp.active_has_tool) x 10. get_active_has_tool (667-672) returns 1.0 for any Tool, with no type or damage check. Nothing in kp's evaluator reads Jasmine's stored effect or Metal Core Barrier's -50: the defender and turn-effect pricing in the threat clock is switched off for kp. Even kd's defender pricing deliberately leaves out Metal Core Barrier and turn effects (hooks/core.rs ~1563-1581).

The traces show it directly. With the official binary, Metal Core Barrier went on the Active Skarmory ex 251 times, but also 57 times on the Active Indeedee ex, which is Psychic, so the -50 can't apply. With the +10 removed, it went on an Active 0 times. A debug replay showed the tool choice as: Active 159.2 against bench 149.2, a gap of exactly 10.

Jasmine gets nothing for its effect, and playing it costs the one-card hand-size term. On 439 of the 1,085 turns it was in hand, the bot played no Supporter at all. Seven of its 8 plays were against Blaziken, whose Hiking Trail refills the hand to 3 at the end of each turn. That makes dumping any card worth +1 in the search.

Wins over 240 games: official 132, no +10 on both sides 97, no +10 on the deck's side only 96, Jasmine priced 146. The drop of about 15 points is about 3 standard errors, so the tools really help once played. The +6 for Jasmine is within noise at this size.
